How to Buy, Store, and Eat a Persimmon | Epicurious
s: December 1, 2016 - Scientists categorize persimmon varieties according to whether they’re astringent when unripe—that is, mouth-wrenchingly bitter—or not. Fuyus are not. They have a firm, mildly sweet flesh that you can eat raw and bake with. They'll stand up in savory dishes, too. Hachiyas, on the other hand, are astringent as all get out. They’re firm like Fuyus when you buy them but—this is crucial—you have to wait until they’re soft to the point of squishy before eating them.
